title: The Harbor of Maple Hollow
premise: Marine biologist Jude Kavanagh returns to Maple Hollow to count sea turtles and nurse a decade-old heartbreak, only to discover her late grandmother's stubborn orchard deed names two heirs: Jude and Callum Reyes, the man who left town without saying goodbye. Forced into shared custody of the orchard, they unearth evidence that the deed was forged to hide an old injustice done to Callum's family, pitting loyalty to the town's founding families against the truth. As the legal deadline to contest the deed approaches, Jude must finally speak the apology she has rehearsed for ten years, and Callum must choose between vengeance and belonging. They keep the orchard together, expose the forgery, and choose each other as the turtles return to the harbor.
about_author: Ines Voss is the pen name of a former coastal researcher who traded tide charts for love stories set in small towns where everyone knows your business. She writes about second chances, stubborn land, and the people who refuse to leave either.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She arrives in Maple Hollow for a seasonal turtle survey, relieved to bury herself in data after a failed engagement. Walking past the overgrown Kavanagh orchard, she learns her grandmother has died and left her the property. Emotional beat: guarded grief disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the county office, lawyer Marisol reveals the deed names a second heir: Callum Reyes, who vanished from town ten years ago without explanation. Jude's stomach drops; he was the boy she loved and lost. Beat: dread wrapped in disbelief.

chapters.title: The Man at the Dock
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He returns to town after his father's death, carrying a box of old letters and a grudge against the Hollow's founding families. He sees Jude on the dock and can't decide whether to flee or stay. Beat: longing colliding with resentment.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol explains the deed: neither heir can sell without the other's consent, and a challenge must be filed within ninety days or the orchard passes to the Whitmore family trust. Jude and Callum agree to a tense truce. Beat: forced proximity, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Ninety Days of Apples
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They begin restoring the neglected orchard, bickering through pruning and irrigation repairs. Old neighbors watch, gossiping. A small kindness—Callum fixing her truck unasked—cracks Jude's armor slightly. Beat: reluctant warmth.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Clearing the root cellar, he finds correspondence between his grandfather and Jude's grandmother suggesting the original Reyes land was taken unfairly decades ago. He hides the letters, unsure whether to use them as ammunition. Beat: temptation of grievance.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Nesting season peaks; Jude invites Callum to help tag hatchlings at night. Working side by side under lantern light, they talk around the past without touching it. Beat: intimacy rekindling despite themselves.

chapters.title: What Happened Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Dual POV flashbacks. The truth surfaces: Callum left because his family was ruined by a Whitmore lawsuit, and Jude chose silence to protect her own family's standing. Each remembers the abandonment differently. Beat: old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: The Whitmores' Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Eleanor Whitmore offers to buy out both heirs generously—if they drop any questions about the land's history. Jude senses fear beneath the courtesy. Beat: first hint that the town's respectability has rot underneath.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A nor'easter flattens half the orchard. Neighbors show up to help rebuild, including people who once shunned the Reyeses. Callum feels the dangerous pull of belonging. Beat: community as seduction.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A visiting archivist confirms the 1970s transfer signature was forged—the same hand appears on documents benefiting the Whitmore trust. Callum wants to go public immediately; Jude urges caution. Beat: alliance strained by different definitions of justice.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts her mother, who admits the family knew and stayed silent to keep their place in the Hollow. Jude realizes her decade of silence began long before Callum left. Beat: shame transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He and Jude break into the closed historical society to copy records before someone destroys them. Caught between alarm bells and adrenaline, they nearly kiss, then don't. Beat: desire deferred, trust deepening.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Warning
chapters.summary: Eleanor's POV (brief) then Jude's. Eleanor threatens a countersuit that would bankrupt them both and reminds Jude what the town did to the last family who spoke up. Jude wavers—until she finds turtle nests threatened by the trust's planned marina. Beat: private stakes become public ones.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the beach at dawn, Jude finally says the sentence she has practiced for ten years: 'I should have chosen you, and I didn't, and I'm sorry.' Callum doesn't forgive her yet—but he stays. Beat: catharsis without resolution.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With days left to file the challenge, evidence disappears from the courthouse, Marisol is pressured off the case, and a fire damages the root cellar. Someone in town is protecting the secret violently. Beat: rising menace.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. An elderly former farmhand comes forward, willing to testify about the forged transfer—if they can protect him. They hide him at the orchard, turning it into the refuge it once was for everyone. Beat: the orchard becomes a symbol of shelter.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The turtle survey data shows the harbor's health collapsing wherever Whitmore development touches it—scientific proof braided with the legal one. Jude decides truth isn't betrayal of the town; it's the only way back in. Beat: themes converge.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the probate hearing, the farmhand testifies, the archivist's documents are entered, and Eleanor's son—wanting out from under his mother's shadow—confirms the forgery. The deed is voided; the orchard belongs to Jude and Callum outright. Beat: justice outside and inside the law at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The town reckons with itself; some doors close, others open. Eleanor retreats but leaves a cryptic warning about the marina fight ahead. Callum asks Jude not for forgiveness but for a future. Beat: quiet, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Autumn: the orchard bears its first real crop in years, sold at a stand run by neighbors who once looked away. Callum plants new trees with his father's name carved on the stakes. Beat: belonging achieved, not granted.

chapters.title: The Harbor of Maple Hollow
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Hatchlings make their run to the sea at dusk while Jude and Callum stand on the dock, hands linked, no longer counting heartbreaks. The next fight looms, but they face it rooted in the orchard and in each other. Beat: hopeful, open-ended peace.
